1) the Cl- channels are directly activated, in a voltage-dependent manner, by Ca2+ binding to sites approximately 1.13 A into the electric field from the intracellular surface of the membrane and 2) the Cl- channel activation process involves two sequential Ca2+ bindings followed by a final Ca2+-independent transition to a conducting conformation.

(1) Ca2+-activated Cl- channel activation in rat parotis acinar cells is a sequential, voltage-dependent, and cooperative process that involves two identical Ca2+ binding sites; (2) the apparent Kd of the Ca2+ binding step decreases with increasing voltage; (3) the voltage dependence of the Kd can be explained by assuming a single Ca2+ binding site that is approximately 13% of the membrane electric field into the cell.
